change.title: 3 changes: Stripe.js: deprecated Payment Intents/Setup Intents/Sources methods removed; initCheckout and initEmbeddedCheckout renamed; elements.update() returns a Promise and more

source.quote: Removes deprecated Payment Intents, Setup Intents, and Sources methods from Stripe.js

tasks.reasoning:
This one task covers all 3 stripe changes that affect this repo. Handle every one of them in this single change set, prove each with your test, and say in finish which you changed and which needed no change.

1. Stripe.js: deprecated Payment Intents/Setup Intents/Sources methods removed; initCheckout and initEmbeddedCheckout renamed; elements.update() returns a Promise (other, effective 2026-03-25)
   Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/dahlia.md
   Quote: Removes deprecated Payment Intents, Setup Intents, and Sources methods from Stripe.js
   Affects: versions: 2026-03-25.dahlia
   Call sites: components/payment/StripePaymentForm.tsx:19 (useStripe() returns the Stripe.js instance. If the form calls a removed deprecated method (confirmCardPayment, handleCardAction, confirmSetup variants, Sources methods), it breaks once Stripe.js is on the Dahlia release.); components/payment/StripePaymentForm.tsx:20 (useElements() is used with the Stripe.js instance. Elements.update() now returns a Promise, and initCheckout/initEmbeddedCheckout were renamed, so check any calls to these.)
   Why it applies: The repo uses @stripe/react-stripe-js 3.6.0 with useStripe/useElements in a payment form. The call-site scan did not read which Stripe.js methods the form calls. This is a client-side change that the server-side stripe-node upgrade does not cover, because it needs its own @stripe/stripe-js and react-stripe-js edit. UNCERTAIN: the migration agent should read StripePaymentForm.tsx and replace any removed Payment Intents, Setup Intents or Sources methods, and await elements.update() if it is used. It should also check whether any initCheckout/initEmbeddedCheckout usage exists elsewhere. If the form only renders Elements and uses supported methods, little may be needed.

2. stripe-node (npm) 23.0.0: pins 2026-09-30.endive; removes Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType export, V2List V1-only fields (sdk-major, effective 2026-09-30)
   Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
   Quote: Removed the function `Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification()` that was mistakenly added in version 22.5.0 of this package.
   Affects: versions: <23.0.0, 23.0.0; sdk: stripe
   Call sites: lib/stripe/getOrCreateCustomer.ts:5 (This explicitly pins apiVersion 2025-04-30.basil. Newer SDK types only accept their own pinned version literal, so the pin must be updated to 2026-09-30.endive or removed.); app/api/stripe/generate-checkout/route.ts:62 (checkout.sessions.create passes payment_method_types, which is removed on 2026-09-30.endive (400 error). Remove it and rely on dynamic payment methods.); app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:20 (webhooks.constructEvent is the correct method for snapshot events, but stripe-node 21+ throws if the wrong parsing method is used for an event type. The removed constructEventWithoutVerification is not used here, so confirm that.); lib/stripe.ts:62 (subscriptions.retrieve response shapes may differ across the Basil to Endive versions (v2 and decimal changes). Check the fields the code reads.); lib/syncStripeDataToKV.ts:6 (subscriptions.list with expand: check the fields read from the response and the expand paths against the new API version.); lib/stripe.ts:1 (This is likely where the Stripe client is constructed (not read by the scan). Under stripe-node 22+ it must use new Stripe(...) rather than calling Stripe() as a function. Verify the actual construction site.)
   Why it applies: The repo uses stripe-node 18.1.0 pinned to API 2025-04-30.basil, so it is behind 19 to 23. The explicit pin keeps current behavior stable, but the SDK is on a version range named by these changes. One upgrade PR to stripe-node 23.0.0 covers the SDK bump, the API version move and the field removals the bump causes. UNCERTAIN: the Stripe client construction site and the response fields read in subscription sync were not read by the scan. The migration agent should check them, plus whether to keep an older explicit apiVersion pin instead of moving to Endive.

3. Stripe.js: payment request button deprecated; handleNextAction UI, canConfirm, address and billing-details validation behaviour changes in Elements (other, effective 2026-09-30)
   Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog.md
   Quote: Deprecates the payment request button
   Affects: operations: elements.create('paymentRequestButton'), stripe.handleNextAction; versions: 2026-09-30.endive
   Call sites: components/payment/StripePaymentForm.tsx:19 (useStripe() could be used for stripe.handleNextAction or to back a payment request button. The scan did not show this, so verify.); components/payment/StripePaymentForm.tsx:20 (useElements() is used with Elements, where address and billing-details validation, canConfirm and handleNextAction UI behavior changed.)
   Why it applies: The repo has a Stripe Elements payment form (react-stripe-js 3.6.0). The changes cover the deprecated payment request button and validation or handleNextAction behavior in Elements. It is unclear whether the form uses paymentRequestButton, handleNextAction or billing-details validation. The migration agent should read StripePaymentForm.tsx and replace any paymentRequestButton with Express Checkout Element and review validation behavior. If none of these are used, no edit is needed. This is a deprecation, so it is low urgency.

callSites.why: useStripe() returns the Stripe.js instance. If the form calls a removed deprecated method (confirmCardPayment, handleCardAction, confirmSetup variants, Sources methods), it breaks once Stripe.js is on the Dahlia release.
useElements() is used with the Stripe.js instance. Elements.update() now returns a Promise, and initCheckout/initEmbeddedCheckout were renamed, so check any calls to these.
This explicitly pins apiVersion 2025-04-30.basil. Newer SDK types only accept their own pinned version literal, so the pin must be updated to 2026-09-30.endive or removed.
checkout.sessions.create passes payment_method_types, which is removed on 2026-09-30.endive (400 error). Remove it and rely on dynamic payment methods.

webhooks.constructEvent is the correct method for snapshot events, but stripe-node 21+ throws if the wrong parsing method is used for an event type. The removed constructEventWithoutVerification is not used here, so confirm that.
subscriptions.retrieve response shapes may differ across the Basil to Endive versions (v2 and decimal changes). Check the fields the code reads.
subscriptions.list with expand: check the fields read from the response and the expand paths against the new API version.

This is likely where the Stripe client is constructed (not read by the scan). Under stripe-node 22+ it must use new Stripe(...) rather than calling Stripe() as a function. Verify the actual construction site.
useStripe() could be used for stripe.handleNextAction or to back a payment request button. The scan did not show this, so verify.
useElements() is used with Elements, where address and billing-details validation, canConfirm and handleNextAction UI behavior changed.

## 3 changes: Stripe.js: deprecated Payment Intents/Setup Intents/Sources methods removed; initCheckout and initEmbeddedCheckout renamed; elements.update() returns a Promise and more [Verified]

### Change

I made no code changes. StripePaymentForm.tsx only renders PaymentElement and calls stripe.confirmPayment({elements, confirmParams, redirect:'if_required'}). I did not run any checks or provider validators.

Files touched:
- `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`

### Why

Change 1 (Stripe.js removals) needs no edit. confirmPayment is not among the removed methods (confirmCardPayment, handleCardAction, Sources). Searching the repo found no calls to initCheckout, initEmbeddedCheckout, elements.update, paymentRequestButton or handleNextAction. Change 3 (payment request button deprecation, Elements validation changes) needs no edit for the same reason. Change 2 (stripe-node 23 and API 2026-09-30.endive) is not forced by these changes. The repo pins stripe@18.1.0 to 2025-04-30.basil explicitly, so it keeps working unchanged. Moving it to stripe-node 23 would be a separate, optional upgrade.

> Removes deprecated Payment Intents, Setup Intents, and Sources methods from Stripe.js

Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/dahlia.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Provider validators: none run.

Prepared before the baseline:
- Checks ran with placeholder env: NEON_DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, GROQ_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, SENDGRID_SECRET_KEY, UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL, UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN, GITHUB_APP_ID, GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET, GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, NEXTAUTH_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL, CRON_SECRET, TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- I did not check whether the installed @stripe/stripe-js or react-stripe-js versions load a Stripe.js release that has these removals.
- I did not upgrade stripe-node to 23. That would also need the apiVersion pin updated, payment_method_types removed from checkout.sessions.create, and a review of subscription fields. All of that is optional, not forced.
- No test of this change was written: No code changed, so there is nothing for a test to prove.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

None intended.

review.summary: The only visible change is a regenerated tsconfig.tsbuildinfo, a build cache artifact. The diff shown (truncated at 60,000 characters) contains no source edits, so it does not address the Stripe.js removals or renames. Judging from the pre-change files, the code never used the removed APIs: StripePaymentForm.tsx uses the supported stripe.confirmPayment({elements,...}) with PaymentElement, and the server routes use stripe-node calls (checkout.sessions.create, billingPortal.sessions.create, webhooks.constructEvent, subscriptions.list/retrieve, customers.create) that this client-side Stripe.js change doesn't touch. No-op may be the correct outcome, but the 'verified' grade rests on typecheck and build passing before and after, which cannot show runtime behavior. The nine named call sites are mostly server-side SDK calls unrelated to the Stripe.js change, so the match looks over-broad. Pre-existing: apiVersion is pinned to 2025-04-30.basil in lib/stripe.ts and getOrCreateCustomer.ts, so the server SDK is not moving to the new API version. I could not see any package.json change in the visible diff, so I can't confirm whether @stripe/stripe-js or @stripe/react-stripe-js versions changed.

It also embeds machine-specific paths (../../../../../../../usr/lib/node_modules/typescript) and creates noisy diffs. Check whether it was already tracked or was added accidentally.

It is unchanged, and confirmPayment with redirect:'if_required' and paymentIntent status handling is not exercised by typecheck or build. If the Stripe.js version is bumped elsewhere, the checkout flow should be verified manually. I could not confirm from the visible diff whether the dependency versions changed.
The webhook path (constructEvent) is listed as affected but has no code change and no test coverage. 'verified' is based only on compile and build, not on a signed-event test.
